events.title: Gutenberg Bible Printing Begins to Circulate
events.description: Traditionally, February 23, 1455 is cited as the date Johannes Gutenberg completed or began publicly circulating his 42-line Bible, the first major book printed in Europe using movable metal type.
events.significance: Movable-type printing revolutionized the spread of knowledge in Europe, fueling the Renaissance, the Reformation, and the Scientific Revolution. Note that the exact date is traditional and not firmly documented.

events.title: Battle of Buena Vista
events.description: During the Mexican-American War, U.S. forces under General Zachary Taylor defeated a much larger Mexican army led by General Antonio López de Santa Anna near Saltillo, Mexico, concluding on February 23.
events.significance: The victory secured northern Mexico for the United States and boosted Zachary Taylor's national reputation, helping propel him to the presidency in 1848.

events.title: Birth of W. E. B. Du Bois
events.description: William Edward Burghardt Du Bois was born in Great Barrington, Massachusetts. He became a sociologist, historian, and activist, and was the first African American to earn a doctorate from Harvard.
events.significance: Du Bois co-founded the NAACP in 1909 and authored The Souls of Black Folk, becoming a foundational figure in the American civil rights movement and Pan-Africanism.

events.title: Raising of the Flag on Iwo Jima
events.description: U.S. Marines raised the American flag on Mount Suribachi during the Battle of Iwo Jima. Joe Rosenthal's photograph of the second flag raising became one of the most famous images of World War II.
events.significance: The image became a symbol of American resolve and sacrifice in the Pacific War and inspired the Marine Corps War Memorial.

events.title: Birth of Modern Internet Pioneer Context: Death of Stan Laurel
events.description: Comedian Stan Laurel, half of the legendary duo Laurel and Hardy, died in Santa Monica, California, on February 23, 1965, at age 74.
events.significance: Laurel's work in early film comedy influenced generations of performers, and his partnership with Oliver Hardy remains one of the most celebrated in cinema history.
